verdict_note: From reading only (no cargo, no build, no test, no GUI, no GPU). The B6 frame mechanics hold: the nineteen titles open popups, every designed node stays in the tree at every level with its availability record as node properties, greyed rows answer frame.menu_unavailable with their lower-case reason code and run nothing, the open menu rebuilds only what changed, the Layers context menu lists menu-bar leaf ids and runs them through the same path as the bar, and leaf mutations carry the viewer's run actor. Availability is computed from live state for the 21 bound leaves (profile from the Folio document, undo/redo history, layers, selection, active tool); the other 1,400-odd leaves are honest typed NOT_IMPLEMENTED_YET. The defects are structural and in the spec examples. F1 (high): the menu is a second hand-written registry with its own predicate beside the egui shell's Viewer::menu_bar, which the same Viewer publishes in state_json shell.menu and which the drive path uses for studio.* ids; the same id is AVAILABLE in one and NOT_IMPLEMENTED_YET in the other in the same document state (MENU-INV-4, STU-SHL-015/016/046). F2 (high): the worked example STU-SHL-020 names (a page-layout document) does not hold, because New Timeline requires container:artboard. F3 to F7 (medium): leaves run a hand-written MenuOp arm instead of the catalog command's arm and drift from it (Ungroup's selection); the keyboard and hover highlight is invisible on greyed rows; the components.json keyboard and pointer contract is missing (Right/Left, type-ahead, Shift+F10, safe triangle, scroll lane); the remedy hop names remedies that do not make the predicate true; several spec rows are claimed beyond the code or neither done nor declared. F8 to F11 are low. Visual: no PNG capture or tree dump of an open menu, cascade, greyed row or tooltip exists for this lane (the test scratch folders are deleted on drop and no capture test opens a menu), so the visual verdict is NOT_INSPECTED.

findings.what: STU-SHL-015 says the menu tree IS a field on the command record, folded by menu_path, with no hand-written menu enum, so that a swarm agent dispatching a command id and an operator clicking its leaf execute the identical arm. STU-SHL-046 and MENU-INV-4 require ONE evaluation feeding every renderer. The lane adds a third table (TREE plus BINDINGS plus NODE_REQUIRES plus remedy_of) next to the egui shell's ShellCommand menu. Both use the same studio.* leaf ids (studio.document.open, save, save_as, close, studio.history.undo, redo, studio.view.zoom_in, studio.workspace.panel.*). Both are live in the native host: GuiFrame::refresh calls Viewer::state_json, which evaluates the egui shell's menu into state.shell.menu, and then menu_eval evaluates menu_tree. The two disagree. The prose is copied too: the Undo and Redo help sentences in BINDINGS are the shell.rs:995-996 sentences, so a change to one leaves the other stale. The lane's V4-06 class reads 'a menu surface with its own gating', but its site list covers native-host only, and shell.rs:897-932, shell.rs:942-1073 and drive.rs:335 are unlisted sites of that class (V4-06: a count mismatch blocks READY_FOR_VALIDATION).
findings.scenario: GuiFrame::open on the PSD fixture. f.menu_bar().find('studio.document.save_as') is NOT_IN_THIS_DOCUMENT NOT_IMPLEMENTED_YET 'not built in this host yet' (the lane asserts it at gui_menu.rs:240-247). f.viewer().state_json()['shell']['menu'] lists the same id as AVAILABLE, because shell.rs:958 needs_doc holds with a document open. A model that drives `studio-harness command --command-id studio.document.save_as` runs it (drive.rs:335-352 opens the shell's save dialog state). A second disagreement, in the record: with nothing to undo, studio.history.undo is NOT_IN_THIS_DOCUMENT in both, with profile_clause 'doc_feature:undo_step' in menu_tree and null in the shell (STU-SHL-019 requires identical content on every path).
findings.fix: There must be one source. The spec-aligned form widens the controls UiDescriptor additively (menu_path, menu_order, requires, help or summary, shortcut_id; the lane may touch controls additively), seeds it from ui_seed plus the designed tree, and folds BOTH the native menu and the egui shell's Viewer::menu_bar from it with the one predicate (SHL-P-08). The minimum form, which the lead must allow because the brief forbids shell.rs edits, makes menu_tree the only evaluation: state_json shell.menu and drive.rs studio.* read and run menu_tree's evaluated nodes for every id both know, and the shell's private predicate goes. Whichever form is chosen, list shell.rs:897-1073 and drive.rs:335-352 in notes.v4_06 with their status.

findings.what: The MenuRun reports a catalog command id, but the leaf never runs that command's arm. It calls Viewer methods from its own match, adds side effects, and skips run_command's typed parameter check and its command_outcome observe frame for a run that records no op (HOST INTEGRATION (5)). The undo steps are named by the Viewer methods ('move_layer <id>' for layer.shift_layer, 'new_layer' for layer.new_raster_layer; the d304a3f2 focused log shows the names), and no test asserts that a step is named for its command. Hide Selection on an already hidden layer reports 'ok' with no step (the test walks around this at gui_menu.rs:350). The '…' leaves Duplicate Layer… and Add Track… run immediately with fixed parameters, and New Timeline silently uses the first shipped preset 'ARRI 1080p 24' (folio sequence_preset/shipped.rs:38), while its help says 'the default preset' and no default is declared.
findings.scenario: Select a group and run OBJECT > Ungroup from the menu: nothing is selected afterwards, and OBJECT > Arrange > Bring Forward is now INAPPLICABLE NEEDS_SELECTION. A model runs layer.ungroup on the same document through drive: the last child stays selected, and the model's next layer command acts on it. The operator and the agent diverge after one identical command id.
findings.fix: Dispatch each bound leaf through the catalog arm: Viewer::run_command(command_id, params) for RUN_COMMANDS rows, or the drive viewer row for viewer rows, with parameters built from the selection. Drop the post-run select(None) and keep the command's own selection policy. A run that changes nothing returns a typed nothing_to_change, not ok. Name each leaf's parameters (preset, track kind and name) in its descriptor, or open its dialog, and record a declared default preset id instead of the first shipped one.

findings.what: An explicit L1 tip (the accessibility request) never dismisses on a press elsewhere, a pointer leave or a focus change. While shown, it takes hits over the controls under it, so presses in its rect go to the tip tree and are dropped (rule 5: a tooltip MUST NOT capture the pointer). A tip on a menu row opens 8 px under the row and covers the rows below it in the same popup. When there is room neither below nor above, the clamp to the window top can put the tip over its own control (rule 3). In the Operator's window no dwell tip ever appears, because the host clock is not fed.
findings.scenario: show_tip on the EDIT title, then click the tab strip under the tip: the click is swallowed and the tip stays.
findings.fix: Hide explicit tips on any press outside the tip and on focus change; let presses on the tip's non-interactive area pass through. Place menu-row tips beside the popup (right edge, flipping left at the window edge). When neither side fits, shrink or skip the tip rather than covering the control. Feed GuiFrame::advance from window.rs (outside owned paths: next lane, as declared).

answers.host_integration: Attribution holds: leaves call Viewer methods on the viewer's run, and the test checks each step's actor and session against the run actor (gui_menu.rs:296-301). Undo steps exist one per mutation but are named by the Viewer method, not the command id, and nothing asserts the names (F3). Observe: menu outcomes are receipt counters only; the catalog arm's command_outcome frame is skipped (F3).
